findings: Initial screening refined: pipeline/dedup.py is processed-itemID JSON tracker, SQL is thought/vector similarity retrieval; neither file-byte scanner nor visual identity. MIT read, no code adopted.
DedupTracker _load catches malformedJSON/OSerror as empty dictionary, conflating corrupt/unreadable state with no previously processed items. JSON shape unvalidated.
Atomic replace prevents partial file visibility but no reload/lock/fsync; two independently loaded trackers can overwrite each other. Runtime control pending.

mark_processed mutates memory before _save; save failure leaves item marked in current instance despite no durable state. cleanup parses UTC-Z string with local-time mktime, potential timezone-dependent expiry.
Reviewed migration match_thoughts has filter argument unused, strict threshold less-than boundary, result cap200; later migrations may replace it so no current-live SQL claim yet.

Original DedupTracker temporary-file controls confirm malformedJSON loads empty, two preloaded instances sequential writes lose first update, failed injected _save leaves is_processed true in memory but false after reload. No concurrent timing required; atomic rename does not solve read-modify-write freshness.

Reviewed historical get_recent_thoughts_with_embeddings has no row cap; historical find_dedup_candidates searches recent outer thoughts against all ages, caps neighbors before symmetric dedup, and keeps growing linear seen_pairs array. This is bounded-neighbor candidate retrieval, not exhaustive duplicate graph. Later migrations must be inspected before attributing live behavior.

pipeline/config.py loads dotenv files at import; inspected as source only. Two fully read pipeline test modules cover thought_stats argument forwarding and morning briefing fallback with mocks; neither exercises DedupTracker durability or lost updates. Other tests remain unreviewed.
